summary: Gibraltar has no forced heirship and applies English-style rules. Trusts are fully recognised and the Hague Trusts Convention was extended to Gibraltar. Private foundations are available under a 2017 law.
family_claims: Gibraltar has an English-style family provision claim; the statute was not identified.
foreign_law_note: Movables follow the law of the deceased's domicile, immovables follow Gibraltar law. There is no choice of nationality law.
trust_note: Hague Convention extended to Gibraltar (1 January 1992 per a Dutch treaty record). Foundations are governed by the Gibraltar private foundations law of 2017; its exact title was not verified.
open_questions: The HCCH status-table page could be read only in an older cached version that does not show territorial extensions; extension dates come from the UK Treaty Series 14 (1992) and a Dutch treaty record, and should be re-checked on hcch.net.
Name of the family provision statute and the foundations law, and trust tax rules.
